items.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: we became good friends. As a matter of fact, Illinois, Joe Newman, and myself we became the unholy three.

ctx.x: Oh, Illinois. When Illinois came from Texas, man, from Houston, you know, he came in -- I think he came to one of our rehearsals. A saxophone player by the name of

Eddie Taylor who was from Houston also and knew Illinois brought him to the rehearsal. And Illinois was playing alto then, he wasn’t playing tenor. And he took his horn out and he played something on his horn man, it just made everybody flip. Jack Kelso, Buddy, damn who’s this -- you know, and we became good friends. As a matter of fact, Illinois, Joe Newman, and myself we became the unholy three. As a mater of fact just before I got engaged to my wife, we were all hanging out. We would always hang out together…
When you say Illinois did something that knocked you guys out, do you remember what it was? What was it, his sound, what he was playing -­

items.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000
items.q: Even as well as Illinois played, as well as Lockjaw played

ctx.x: It’s almost like to recreate what that was you would have had to set aside all your experiences from then on to try to get back to that.

Exactly. It’s not putting Fred or Buddy down or putting anybody down, it’s just that I’m a different person. And my newest, the “Timely” album, is living proof of hey, you might not like it as well but hey what the hell, it’s what I’m doing now. Somebody likes it because it’s been moving. And I’m still doing it and I’m still playing all over the world, which is cool. But it’s like how many Benny Goodman bands really did it? How many Count Basie bands did it? How many Duke Ellington bands did it? Regardless of the…
